summary: Preserve the ReferenceError produced by accessing this before super() in a derived constructor.

target.notes: Represent the derived `this` binding as uninitialized until successful super construction; every pre-super access must check that state.

caveats: C# requires the base constructor invocation before the derived constructor body, so arbitrary pre-super statements require restructuring beyond a normal C# constructor initializer.

tests.name: this before super throws
tests.input: class B {} class D extends B { constructor(){ console.log(this); super(); } } new D();

tests.name: edge: side effect before super without this is allowed
tests.input: class B {} class D extends B { constructor(){ console.log('x'); super(); } } new D();
tests.expected_behavior: prints x, then constructs D; a lowering must preserve this ordering
